title: Electron Coherence and Dephasing by Quasi-Static Coulomb Fluctuations in Classical Ionic Media
abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of quantum-particle propagation through quasi-static electrostatic fluctuations of a classical one-component plasma. The RPA potential is Gaussian but has an unscreened $1/r$ correlation tail, which makes the disorder-averaged retarded Green function infrared sensitive. Its eikonal attenuation scale is $\ell_{\rm w}=k^2/G$ for $g=G/k^3\ll1$, with the formal strong-saddle asymptote $\ell_{\rm s}=(4\sqrt[3]{2}/3)G^{-1/3}$ for $g\gg1$. For a slab of thickness $d$, the retarded--advanced mutual-coherence kernel is infrared finite: the coherence decays algebraically for $λ_D\llρ\ll d$ and saturates at larger transverse separation. Thus equilibrium ionic-density fluctuations constitute a distinct quasi-static dephasing channel with a nonexponential coherence law. A finite coherence radius exists only when the saturation threshold is crossed. Relativistic paraxial reduction gives $a_{\rm rel}=1/(\hbar v)$ and the finite high-energy limit $1/(\hbar c)$. The ionic contribution is very small at conventional TEM energies for a $100\,\mathrm{nm}$ water-like layer. Within the quasi-static model it grows for thicker samples and lower-energy electrons, while sub-keV transmission through liquid water is strongly limited by inelastic scattering.
